rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 L7: "Come to Module 1 with the repo picked, the curated skills installed, and one trivial bug." reads as a teaser/preview of the page's own headings (chunk 2 "1. Pick THE repo", chunk 5 "4. Extract the bundle and install the curated skills"), using generic definite reference (your repo, skills to be installed) rather than a pointer to a specific already-named entity — no ambiguity for a cold reader, self-evident as "a/your repo". Checked every other chunk for pronoun/demonstrative antecedents (chunk 3 L40 "the repo you just picked" resolves to chunk 2; chunk 5 L53 "the repo" likewise): all resolve within prior chunks of this file.

chunk 2 L34: "[build one from zero](trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/build-a-project-from-zero.md)" and chunk 7 L76 "Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering]..." are both navigational pointers named by title, not located by position — satisfies the rule-2 carve-out. Grepped body for positional cross-file phrasing ("the opening lecture", "earlier module", "that story") — zero hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 (L15-18) carries four bold handles, one per bullet (**Trivial bug**, **A small multi-file task**, **A small feature**, **A bigger piece**), each a task-size floor/ceiling label. Maintainer note at L96 frames this exact section as the page's `check_pedagogy.md §34` task-sizing inventory ("each bullet states its own ceiling in prose"), matching §9's own named exception for bolded task-sizing callouts by function, not wording — so the per-slide ≤1 budget doesn't bind this chunk. chunk 7 (L76) "**Read:**" matches the rule's own worked example for the reading-list waiver (mode word bolded, title plain) verbatim. No other chunk carries more than one bold element (chunk 3's "**Session**" is the Session-widget marker per widgets.md, not narrative bold).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework is a procedural setup page, not an exercise or lecture; every heading is imperative or a phase/step label ("1. Pick THE repo", "2. Open a Claude Code session in that repo", "5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness") consistent with the rule's exercise-grammar convention. No heading makes a law-style claim, and none needs to — there is no consolidation/law beat on this page to earn a declarative header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 L70: "*Small steer, small trick. A minute here, another there.*" is the line closest to the aphorism-kicker shape (class c), but it restates neither the chunk's own header ("5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness") nor a `**The point:**` line — there isn't one on this page — so it doesn't match the rule's specific failure shape (closing by restating). Read every bullet across all 9 chunks for doctrine restatement and self-referential design commentary (classes a, b) — none found; every bullet states a distinct task, criterion, or artefact.
